# Purgatorium (p9m)

> Self-hosted sandboxes for your team and their AI agents

Purgatorium (p9m) gives each user of a team their own Docker daemon on demand: a sandbox with Portainer, a public URL for every app, sleep when idle and wake on the next request, archive on delete. A REST API and an MCP server (at /mcp) let coding agents create, wake and deploy to sandboxes.

# Getting started

# Install

No git clone is needed: every file comes from a GitHub release, and the image carries the rest.

First check the machine; it changes nothing (give it the `HOST_DOMAIN` you plan to use):

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/releases/latest/download/check-host.sh | bash -s -- dev.example.com
```

Or download it, read it, then run it:

```
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/releases/latest/download/check-host.sh
less check-host.sh
bash check-host.sh dev.example.com
```

Then, on a Linux host with Docker Engine and the compose plugin (Compose 2.17 or newer):

```
mkdir p9m && cd p9m
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/releases/latest/download/docker-compose.yml
curl -fsSL https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/releases/latest/download/setup.sh | bash -s -- dev.example.com   # .env with your domain and random secrets
docker compose up -d
```

The directory must be called `p9m`: the compose project name comes from it. For a given version, use `releases/download/v0.5.0/…` instead of `releases/latest/download/…`.

`check-host.sh` checks Docker and Docker Compose, sysbox, the address pools, ports, disk and registry access, and changes nothing (its sysbox check runs one throw-away `alpine` container); with the `HOST_DOMAIN` you plan to use it also checks the DNS records and, if `certs/` has one, the certificate. Lines marked ✘ must be fixed first, ⚠ are worth reading.

`setup.sh` works in the current directory: it creates `.env` from its release's `env.example`, sets `HOST_DOMAIN` to the domain you give it and `PUBLIC_URL` to `p9m.<domain>` (`https://` if `certs/` already holds a certificate, else `http://`: run it again with the domain after adding one; a `PUBLIC_URL` you set yourself is kept), fills in random secrets, creates `data/`, `opt/`, `certs/` and `dynamic/`, and prints the admin password and token. It keeps values you already set, so it is safe to run again. Without it: download `env.example` of the release as `.env` and set `HOST_DOMAIN`, `PUBLIC_URL` and the three secrets by hand.

`docker compose up -d` pulls the released image `ghcr.io/csakaszamok/p9m`. It carries the sandbox templates and runtimes, and the files the other services read: on every `up` the one-shot `p9m-init` service copies the Sablier themes, the error pages, the registry config and `dynamic/errors.yml` from it, so they always match the running version. To work on the code, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/csakaszamok/p9m/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

The stack runs Traefik v3.6 with the Sablier plugin, Sablier, a registry and the Purgatorium API. The UI is at `http://p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>` (by default `http://p9m.lvh.me`, which resolves to `127.0.0.1`), the API also on port `8081` of the host.

An app takes seconds to open the first time?

In Chrome, *Settings → Privacy and security → Security → Use secure DNS*: with "your current service provider" each new `*.lvh.me` name can wait for a slow or filtering resolver. Turn it off, or pick a provider such as Cloudflare (1.1.1.1).

Each sandbox's files (compose file, certificates, tunnel config) live in `opt/sandboxes/<owner>/<name>/`, its archives in `opt/archive/<owner>/`; `<owner>` is `admin` or the user's sign-in e-mail.

> **Give the Docker daemon a larger address pool.** Every sandbox — sleeping ones included — keeps its own compose network until it is archived. Docker's default pools only allow about 30 networks; beyond that sandbox creation fails with `fully subnetted`. Set smaller subnets in the daemon config (`/etc/docker/daemon.json`, or Docker Desktop → Settings → Docker Engine) and restart Docker:
>
> ```
> { "default-address-pools": [ { "base": "10.10.0.0/16", "size": 28 } ] }
> ```
>
> A sandbox network needs only a handful of addresses, so `/28` subnets are enough: this allows 4096 networks (`/24` would allow 256).
>
> **Before exposing Purgatorium publicly**, set `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `SESSION_SECRET` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` to real secrets. The compose defaults (`ADMIN_TOKEN=abc123`, and the `.env.example` placeholders) are only meant for local dev and the e2e scripts; Purgatorium logs a startup warning if any of them is still in effect.

All settings: [Configuration](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/configuration/index.md). For HTTPS: [HTTPS](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/https/index.md).

# First sandbox

```
# Create a sandbox
curl -X POST http://localhost:8081/sandboxes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name": "alice", "idle_timeout": "30m"}'

# Response (abridged)
{
  "name": "p9m-alice",
  "tunnel_urls": ["alice-inner-http-echo-port5678.lvh.me", "..."],
  "registry_url": "registry.lvh.me",
  "registry_username": "alice",
  "registry_password": "...",
  "docker_access": { "host": "alice-docker.lvh.me", "state": "ready" },
  "extras": {}
}
```

Sign in at `http://p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>` to create sandboxes in the browser or mint a personal access token for your agents.

With `"template": "portainer"` the sandbox also gets Portainer, and `extras` has its `portainer_url` and `portainer_password`.

# Configuration

Main settings in `.env`:

| Variable                                                                    | Default                                               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ADMIN_TOKEN`                                                               | `abc123` (dev only)                                   | Bearer token with admin rights on the API                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `ADMIN_USER`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`                                              | `admin`, —                                            | The local admin account of the UI                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `SESSION_SECRET`                                                            | —                                                     | Signs the session cookie; a long random string                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `HOST_DOMAIN`                                                               | `lvh.me`                                              | Every address is under it: the UI, the registry, the sandbox apps (needs a wildcard DNS record)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `HOST_ADDRESS`                                                              | `localhost`                                           | The host's address, put into the sandbox TLS certificates and used for the registry token URL when `PUBLIC_URL` is not set                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `UI_HOST`                                                                   | `p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>`                                   | The UI's own address, e.g. `console.example.com` with `HOST_DOMAIN=example.com`: the sandbox apps stay `<sandbox>-<subdomain>.example.com`. Under `HOST_DOMAIN`, the wildcard DNS record and certificate cover it. Set `PUBLIC_URL` to it too, and register its `/auth/callback` with the OIDC provider. A sandbox whose apps' addresses would include it (a sandbox `console` with `console-admin.example.com`) cannot be created                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `PUBLIC_URL`                                                                | `http://<UI_HOST>`                                    | The address of the UI as users see it; `https://…` turns on the HTTPS checks (see [HTTPS](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/https/index.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `OIDC_ISSUER`, `OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, `OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME` | —                                                     | Sign-in for everyone but the admin (see [Web UI and sign-in](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/web-ui/index.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`, `OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS`                               | — (anyone)                                            | Who may sign in with OIDC, as comma lists: domains (`example.com,partner.org`, the exact domain, not its subdomains) and single addresses (`guest@gmail.com`). Without either, anyone with an account at the provider can sign in, with Google any Google account; Purgatorium says so in its log at startup. Checked at sign-in and on every request: someone taken off the list (after a restart) is signed out and their tokens stop working at once. The admin is never limited                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `OIDC_ADMIN_EMAILS`                                                         | — (none)                                              | Addresses (comma list) that are the admin when they sign in with OIDC in the browser, as the local admin is: all sandboxes, the Overview, users, no limits, host folders. They may sign in even if `OIDC_ALLOWED_*` leaves them out. Their tokens stay a user's. Taken off the list (after a restart), their session is a user's again at once. The local admin (`ADMIN_USER`) stays                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `APPS_ACCESS_DEFAULT`                                                       | `public`                                              | Who opens a sandbox app without a `p9m.access` label: `public`, `domain` (anyone who can sign in to Purgatorium) or `owner` (see [App access](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/app-access/index.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `APP_ACCESS_SECRET`                                                         | generated into `data/app-access.key`                  | Signs the app access cookies and sign-in tickets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `HUB_ENABLED`                                                               | `false`                                               | The [Hub](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/hub/index.md), the team's published apps at their own address: off unless `true`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `HUB_HOST`                                                                  | `hub.<HOST_DOMAIN>`                                   | The Hub's address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `HUB_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`, `HUB_ALLOWED_EMAILS`                                 | (empty)                                               | Who may look at the Hub besides the builders (`OIDC_ALLOWED_*`): viewers, who cannot sign in to Purgatorium itself. Empty: only builders.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `HUB_TITLE`                                                                 | `Hub`                                                 | Shown in the Hub's header.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `SANDBOX_QUOTA`                                                             | `3`                                                   | Sandboxes a user may have running at once; asleep and deep-sleeping ones are not counted; `0` = unlimited                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `SANDBOX_QUOTA_MAX`                                                         | (empty)                                               | How many a user may have running while the server has room, above the guaranteed `SANDBOX_QUOTA` (e.g. `10`). Above the guarantee a new sandbox, or one woken, needs room to spare: every other owner must still be able to reach their guarantee (their running sandboxes hold their places already), and so must one newcomer. Waking from plain sleep takes no new place, so only this maximum counts. Nobody is ever put to sleep to make room. Empty: nothing above `SANDBOX_QUOTA`; `0`: no maximum                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `FILES_MAX_UPLOAD`                                                          | `100m`                                                | The largest file the **Files** tab (and `PUT /sandboxes/:name/files/content`) takes, like `512m` or `1g`. Every request body is read into memory first, so this (plus 1 MB) is also the cap on any request: a larger one gets 413                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `SANDBOX_MAX_TOTAL`                                                         | `200` (`setup.sh`: the suggested number for the host) | Running sandboxes on the whole server, the admin's included. The suggested number: twice as many as can all use their full `SANDBOX_CPUS` and `SANDBOX_MEMORY` at once (2 GB of memory kept for the rest), since most idle or sleep at any moment and a full server asks people to put theirs to sleep; at most as many as the disk holds at `SANDBOX_DISK` each. `setup.sh` writes it into a new `.env` in place of the example's 200, `check-host.sh` prints it, and the admin's Overview shows it under Host resources, with a warning when the limit set is well above it; asleep, deep-sleeping and archived ones take no place, so letting a sandbox sleep frees it for everyone. When it is reached nobody but the admin can create one or wake one: the admin is never refused, but its running sandboxes take places too; `0` = no limit. Each sandbox, asleep too, keeps a Docker network until it goes into deep sleep: the host's Docker address pools must have room for them (see `check-host.sh`) |
| `DEFAULT_RUNTIME`                                                           | `auto`                                                | Runtime for new sandboxes when a request names none: `auto` picks `sysbox` where the host has sysbox installed (no privileged container) and `dind` otherwise; or name one (see [Runtimes and templates](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/runtimes-templates/index.md))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ALLOWED_RUNTIMES`                                                          | — (all)                                               | Runtimes new sandboxes may use, as a comma list: `sysbox` forbids the privileged `dind` on a shared server. Others are left out of `GET /runtimes` and the **New sandbox** form, and a create asking for one is a 400 (so is one without a runtime when the default is not allowed). Existing sandboxes keep running, sleeping and waking                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `SANDBOX_CPUS`, `SANDBOX_MEMORY`                                            | `2`, `4g`                                             | CPU and memory limit of every new sandbox (see [CPU and memory](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/resources/#cpu-and-memory))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `SANDBOX_MAX_CPUS`, `SANDBOX_MAX_MEMORY`                                    | `4`, `8g`                                             | How far a user can raise their sandbox's limits; the admin can go up to the host                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `SANDBOX_MAX_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `SANDBOX_MAX_DEEP_SLEEP_AFTER`                  | — (no limit)                                          | How long a user's sandbox may stay awake without traffic, and asleep before deep sleep, at most (e.g. `2h`, `1d`); with a limit, *never* (`off`) is not allowed either. A template's longer default is cut to it; a sandbox that already has a longer value keeps it until it is changed. The admin is not limited                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `SANDBOX_DISK`                                                              | `20g`                                                 | Disk use above which a sandbox is flagged; a warning only, see [Disk](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/resources/#disk)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `HOST_MOUNT_ROOTS`                                                          | (empty: off)                                          | Host folders the admin may mount into a sandbox, as a comma list of absolute paths (e.g. `/srv/shared,/data/projects`): a mount's host path must be one of them or under one (`/srv/shared2` is not under `/srv/shared`). Entries that are not absolute or have `..` are ignored, with a warning at startup; `/` (the whole host) is allowed, with a warning. **A mount gives whoever owns the sandbox that host folder, as root** (read-only if mounted so), and to every app in it. Empty: nobody can add a mount; ones already there stay until the admin removes them. See [Host folders](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/web-ui/#host-folders)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `LOGIN_CAPACITY`                                                            | `on`                                                  | The sign-in page shows the sandbox places on the server: taken and free of `SANDBOX_MAX_TOTAL`, with a bar (orange from 90%, red when full). The page is public, so `off` hides it; nothing is shown without a server limit. Counted at most every 30 seconds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `GITHUB_STATS`                                                              | `on`                                                  | The topbar links to the GitHub repo and shows Purgatorium's version, stars and forks; the admin also sees when a newer release is out (one of the running series, else a later series). The server fetches the counts and the releases at most once an hour (users' browsers never contact GitHub, and nothing about the installation is sent); `off` never asks GitHub, and the link and the version stay                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `USER_VIEW_SWITCH`                                                          | `false`                                               | `true` gives users the \*\*Simple                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `GITHUB_LINK`                                                               | `on`                                                  | `off` takes the GitHub card out of the topbar (and GitHub is never asked for the counts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `UI_TITLE`                                                                  | `Purgatorium`                                         | The name at the top left, on the sign-in page and in the browser tab titles; `none` shows no name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `UI_LOGO`                                                                   | Purgatorium's logo                                    | The logo next to the name and the browser tab icon, on the Hub too: an `https://` address, or an image file in the container (`.svg`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.webp`, `.gif`, `.ico`), e.g. `/app/data/logo.png` for `./data/logo.png`, served as `/assets/custom-logo`; `none` shows no logo. Its height is fixed, its width follows the image                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`                                                          | `starter`                                             | Template for new sandboxes when a request names none. An old value such as `dind-standard` makes every create without a template fail with `Unknown template`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `DEEP_SLEEP_CHECK_INTERVAL`                                                 | `1m`                                                  | How often Purgatorium looks for sandboxes to take into deep sleep                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `HOST_SANDBOXES_DIR`                                                        | auto-detected                                         | Host path of `opt/sandboxes` (every sandbox's compose file mounts from it). Set it only if auto-detection fails                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `P9M_API_BIND`                                                              | `0.0.0.0`                                             | Interface of the direct API port `8081`; `127.0.0.1` for a public deployment                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `P9M_VERSION`                                                               | the release the `docker-compose.yml` came from        | The image version to run. Pin it only to stay on a version: an upgrade with a new `docker-compose.yml` then needs it changed too                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `REGISTRY_PUBLIC_PULL`                                                      | `true`                                                | Images whose versions all passed the secret scan can be pulled without a login; `false`: tokens only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `REGISTRY_CACHE_TTL`                                                        | `720h` (30 days)                                      | How long the sandboxes' Docker Hub cache (`registry-cache`) keeps an image, counted from its **first** download: pulling it again does not extend it, so an image is downloaded again once its time is up, even in the middle of a workshop. In hours (`168h` = 7 days); `0` keeps everything for ever (the cache only grows: watch the disk). Not in hours (e.g. `7d`): the cache does not start, and the sandboxes pull from Docker Hub directly                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

# HTTPS

Purgatorium serves HTTPS with a certificate you copy in (no automatic issuing):

1. Copy a wildcard certificate for `*.<HOST_DOMAIN>` (ideally also `<HOST_DOMAIN>`) to `certs/tls.crt` (PEM, full chain: certificate + intermediates) and its key to `certs/tls.key` (PEM, unencrypted). `certs/` is git-ignored.
1. Set `PUBLIC_URL=https://p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>` and strong `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `SESSION_SECRET` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `.env`.
1. `docker compose up -d p9m traefik`. At startup Purgatorium writes `dynamic/tls.yml` (the certificate + an HTTP→HTTPS redirect for every host); Traefik serves the UI, API, registry and every sandbox app on port 443.

To renew, overwrite the two files and run `docker compose restart traefik`. Remove them and restart Purgatorium (`docker compose up -d p9m`) to go back to plain HTTP.

## Trying it locally with HTTPS (e.g. on Windows)

With `PUBLIC_URL=https://p9m.lvh.me` but no certificate in `certs/`, Traefik answers with its own self-signed one: the browser says *Not secure*, and although you can click through for the pages, it refuses the connections pages open themselves — the browser **Terminal** stays *disconnected*. (`lvh.me` and every `*.lvh.me` resolve to 127.0.0.1, so nothing else is needed.) Make a certificate your machine trusts with [mkcert](https://github.com/FiloSottile/mkcert). In PowerShell:

```
winget install FiloSottile.mkcert
# winget changes PATH for new shells only: pick it up in this one
$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','Machine') + ';' + [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User')
mkcert -install                     # adds a local CA to Windows' trusted roots (confirm the dialog)
cd <your p9m checkout>
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force certs | Out-Null
mkcert -cert-file certs\tls.crt -key-file certs\tls.key "*.lvh.me" lvh.me
docker compose restart p9m traefik
```

Then close the browser completely and open `https://p9m.lvh.me` again. On macOS / Linux the same with `brew install mkcert` / your package manager, and `certs/tls.crt`, `certs/tls.key`. The TLS TCP addresses (`psql`, SSH) use this certificate too, so their *self-signed certificate* warnings go away. Firefox keeps its own trust store: `mkcert -install` covers it when `certutil` (NSS tools) is installed.

For a public deployment also set `P9M_API_BIND=127.0.0.1` (the direct plain-HTTP API port 8081 is then only reachable on the host) — with `PUBLIC_URL` set, docker clients get registry tokens from `$PUBLIC_URL/v2/auth`, i.e. over HTTPS.

With an `https://` `PUBLIC_URL`, Purgatorium **refuses to start** while `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `SESSION_SECRET` or `ADMIN_PASSWORD` is a default or `.env.example` value (or `SESSION_SECRET` is unset). A running sandbox whose address no router matches shows "This address does not reach the sandbox" instead of an endless waiting page.
# Tutorials

# Tutorials

Step by step, from nothing to an app with a link you can send to anyone. No server knowledge needed: your coding agent does the technical part.

- **[Put your app online with Claude Code](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/tutorials/claude-code/index.md)**: install the p9m plugin once, approve each project in the browser, then say *deploy this app*. The easiest way.
- **[Put your app online with any agent](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/tutorials/other-agents/index.md)**: Codex, Cursor, or Claude Code without the plugin, with a zip from Purgatorium.
- **[Share your app with your team on the Hub](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/tutorials/hub/index.md)**: list it where colleagues find, open and vote for it.

You need a Purgatorium account: the address your team uses (for example `https://p9m.example.com`) and a sign-in. Someone in your team set Purgatorium up; to set up your own, see [Install](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/install/index.md).

# Put your app online with Claude Code

You have an app on your computer (a website, a dashboard, a small tool) and you want a link to it that works for anyone. Claude Code builds and runs it in your Purgatorium sandbox and gives you that link.

**What you need:** Claude Code (in a terminal, or the **Code** tab of the Claude desktop app), [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) installed on your computer, and a Purgatorium account.

## 1. Make a sandbox

1. Open your Purgatorium address in the browser and sign in.
1. Click **+ New sandbox**, give it a short name (for example `shop`), keep the template and click **Create**. It takes 10–30 seconds.

A sandbox is your own small server: your app runs there, not on your computer.

Simple or Advanced

The switch at the top right changes how much the screen shows. **Simple** is enough for everything here. If you see no switch, you are in Simple: the server lets only the admin switch.

## 2. Install the p9m plugin in Claude Code (once)

1. In Purgatorium, click your sandbox, then **Let your agent deploy…**.

1. In the window's step **1**, click **Copy** next to each of the two lines, open a terminal (in VS Code: **Terminal → New Terminal**; on Windows also PowerShell, on a Mac the Terminal app), paste them one after the other and press Enter after each:

   ```
   claude plugin marketplace add csakaszamok/p9m
   claude plugin install p9m@p9m
   ```

   It installs the plugin for you, in all your projects. It asks for no address and no token.

Good to know

- `claude` not found? Claude Code is not installed for the terminal: see [Claude Code's setup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup). An *unknown option* means an older Claude Code: run `claude update`.
- Already in Claude Code? **In Claude Code instead** in the same window shows the same two lines as `/plugin marketplace add csakaszamok/p9m` and `/plugin install p9m@p9m`. (The Claude Code panel in VS Code has no `/plugin`: use the terminal.)

You install the plugin once. Each project then gets its sandbox in the next step.

## 3. Connect your project folder to the sandbox (once per folder)

Claude Code needs to know which sandbox belongs to which folder. You tell it once per folder; after that it remembers.

1. Open your app's folder in Claude Code: start `claude` in that folder, or open the folder in VS Code or the desktop app.

1. In Purgatorium, in the **Let your agent deploy…** window, step **2**, click **Copy**. Paste the line into Claude Code and press Enter. It looks like this, with your Purgatorium's address and your sandbox's name:

   ```
   /p9m:init https://p9m.example.com shop
   ```

1. Claude Code answers with a link and a code, for example:

   > Open **https://p9m.example.com/activate?code=TGMH-BSGQ** and approve the code **TGMH-BSGQ**.

1. Open the link in your browser (sign in if Purgatorium asks). The page shows the code and the sandbox. Check that the code is the same one Claude Code printed, then click **Approve**.

1. Go back to Claude Code. Within a few seconds it says the folder is connected to the sandbox. That is all.

Approve only your own code

Approve a code only if you just ran `/p9m:init` yourself and Claude Code shows that same code. If someone sends you a link like this, do not approve it: whoever started that code would get into your sandbox. Click **Deny** instead.

What happened behind the scenes: Claude Code got a token for this one sandbox and the sandbox's Docker keys, and wrote them into a `.p9m` folder in your project. You never see or copy them. The folder is secret, and it keeps itself out of git on its own: leave it there. The token works for 90 days (then run `/p9m:init` again). You can revoke it in Purgatorium: Advanced → **Access tokens**, where it is named `Claude Code init <date>`.

If something goes wrong

- **The code ran out:** it works for 10 minutes and only once. Run the same `/p9m:init` line again for a new code.
- **You clicked Deny by mistake:** run `/p9m:init` again.
- **The button says *Enable Docker access and approve*:** the sandbox does not let Docker in yet. Click it: the sandbox restarts (about 30 seconds) and Claude Code carries on by itself.
- **The folder was connected to another sandbox already:** Claude Code asks before it replaces that connection.
- **A wrong sandbox in the list:** if the line names a sandbox that is not yours, the page lets you pick one of your own sandboxes instead.

## 4. Deploy

In the same folder, say in your own words:

> Deploy this app.

Claude Code wakes the sandbox, builds your app there, starts it and checks that it answers. At the end it gives you a link like `https://shop-web.example.com` (your sandbox's name first). Open it: that is your app, and it works for anyone you send it to.

## 5. Change and update

Changed something? Say:

> Update the app.

The same link shows the new version a few seconds later.

## Good to know

- **Sleep:** when nobody uses the app for a while (30 minutes by default), the sandbox sleeps to free the server. The next visit wakes it in a few seconds: the visitor sees *waking up* and then your app. Nothing is lost.
- **Sleep later:** *let it sleep only after 2 hours without visitors* works too, or set it in Purgatorium: the sandbox → **Details** → **Sleep** → **Change…** (*never* is there as well).
- **It does not answer?** Ask Claude Code *why does my app not answer?*: it reads the app's logs in the sandbox. The usual cause is an app that listens only on `localhost`; Claude Code fixes that.
- **Only for you or your colleagues?** Say *make it visible only to me* (or *only to my colleagues*): Claude Code sets `p9m.access` ([App access](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/app-access/index.md)), and opening the link then asks the visitor to sign in to Purgatorium.
- **Docker is needed on your computer** only for its command line: the build runs in the sandbox.

## More projects

Each folder is tied to one sandbox by its own `.p9m` folder, so different folders can use different sandboxes, even on different Purgatorium servers. For another folder, do step 3 there: in Purgatorium, on that folder's sandbox, **Let your agent deploy…**, copy the `/p9m:init` line and paste it into Claude Code in that folder. The plugin needs no new setup.

To move a folder to another sandbox, run that sandbox's `/p9m:init` line in the folder: Claude Code asks, then replaces the connection.

Used the earlier plugin, which asked for an address and a token? Run `/plugin marketplace update p9m` once, then `/p9m:init` in each project.

More details: [Claude Code plugin](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/claude-plugin/index.md).

# Put your app online with any agent

For Codex, Cursor, Claude Code without the plugin, or any agent that can run commands on your computer. You download a small zip from Purgatorium; the agent uses it to build and run your app in your sandbox, and gives you its link.

**What you need:** the agent, [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) installed on your computer, and a Purgatorium account with a sandbox (**+ New sandbox** in Purgatorium; see [step 1 of the Claude Code tutorial](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/tutorials/claude-code/#1-make-a-sandbox)).

## 1. Download the zip

In Purgatorium, click your sandbox, then **Let your agent deploy…** → **Download**; in the Advanced view the same window also has **Options** (the token's name and expiry, a zip without the Docker keys, **Copy as .env**). You get `p9m-<sandbox>.zip`.

It holds a token for this sandbox and its keys: treat it like a password. Do not email it or commit it.

## 2. Hand it to the agent

Open your app's folder with the agent and say:

> Set up the p9m zip from my Downloads in this project and deploy.

The agent unpacks it into a `.p9m` folder in your project, deletes the zip, builds your app in the sandbox, starts it and gives you its link. The `.p9m` folder keeps itself out of git on its own (it has its own `.gitignore`); leave it there, the agent uses it for every later update.

If the agent does not know what to do, point it to the instructions inside: *read .p9m/README.md and deploy this app to my sandbox*.

## 3. Update

Changed something? *Update the app in my sandbox.* The same link shows the new version.

## Good to know

- The zip's token expires in 90 days (in the Advanced view you can choose 30 days or never). Download a new zip then.
- Lost the zip, or someone else got it? In Purgatorium (Advanced view): the sandbox → **Access** → **Rotate Docker keys…** makes the old keys useless, and **Access tokens** lets you revoke its token.
- Sleep and wake work the same as with Claude Code: see [Good to know](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/tutorials/claude-code/#good-to-know) there.

For agent builders: everything the agent does is in the [agent guide](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/agent-guide/index.md).

# Share your app with your team on the Hub

The Hub is your team's showcase: a page at `https://hub.<your Purgatorium domain>` where colleagues find the apps you published, open them with one click, and vote for the ones they like. Colleagues who only use apps can sign in to the Hub alone.

**What you need:** an app already online in your sandbox (see [Put your app online with Claude Code](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/tutorials/claude-code/index.md)), and the Hub turned on in your Purgatorium (ask whoever runs it; it is `HUB_ENABLED=true`).

## 1. Publish

Tell your agent:

> Publish the web app on the Hub, titled "Stock room", described as "Who took what from the stock room".

It adds labels to the app's service in its compose file and deploys again:

```
services:
  web:
    labels:
      p9m.publish: "true"
      p9m.title: "Stock room"
      p9m.description: "Who took what from the stock room"
```

Within about a minute and a half the app is on the Hub. In Purgatorium its **Apps** tab marks it **On the Hub**.

## 2. A picture on its card

> Use /screenshot.png as its Hub image.

That adds `p9m.image: "/screenshot.png"`: a picture the app itself serves (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 2 MB). Without it the Hub uses the page's own preview image, if it has one, or the title's first letter.

## 3. Share

Send colleagues the Hub's address. They see whether your app is running or asleep; **Open** wakes it if it sleeps. Everyone signed in can vote once for each app, yours too.

To take it off the Hub: *remove the app from the Hub* (the agent removes `p9m.publish`), or archive the sandbox.

All labels and settings: [Hub](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/hub/index.md).
# Using Purgatorium

# Web UI and sign-in

Purgatorium has a small web UI (`http://p9m.<HOST_DOMAIN>`, or `UI_HOST`) for creating and managing sandboxes without the API directly, alongside the REST API.

Two ways to sign in:

- **Admin**: a local account, set via `ADMIN_USER` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD`. Signs in with the "Administrator sign-in" form and sees every sandbox (My area + All sandboxes).
- **Everyone else**: OIDC (Google or any OpenID Connect provider). Configure `OIDC_ISSUER`, `OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` and register the redirect URI `$PUBLIC_URL/auth/callback` with the provider — character for character (scheme, no trailing slash), under Google's *Authorized redirect URIs*, otherwise sign-in fails with `redirect_uri_mismatch`. Google accepts `http://` redirect URIs only for `localhost`, so with Google use an `https://` `PUBLIC_URL` (locally: a self-signed `*.lvh.me` certificate in `certs/` and `PUBLIC_URL=https://p9m.lvh.me`, see [HTTPS](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/https/index.md)). `OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME` labels the sign-in button (default `Google`). Signed-in users only see their own sandboxes.

`SESSION_SECRET` signs the session cookie — set it to a long random string; sessions issued under an old value stop working if it changes.

Anyone with an account at the OIDC provider can sign in and create sandboxes, unless `OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` or `OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAILS` limits it (e.g. to `example.com`): with Google, set one of them, or any Google account gets in. An account not on the list is told so on the sign-in page; one taken off the list is signed out, and its tokens stop working, once Purgatorium restarts with the new list. Each user may have `SANDBOX_QUOTA` sandboxes running at once (default 3, `0` = unlimited), guaranteed, and with `SANDBOX_QUOTA_MAX` more while the server has room to spare for the others' guarantees (*Running 4 / 3 · up to 10* beside **New sandbox**); asleep, deep-sleeping and archived ones are not counted, so letting a sandbox sleep frees its place, and the admin is not limited. At the limit a user can neither create a sandbox nor wake one, from sleep or deep sleep: its address shows *Running limit reached*, its address shows *Running limit reached* with the running sandboxes, and **Wake** in the panel lets the owner put one to sleep instead (`POST /sandboxes/:name/start` with `{"sleep": "<name>"}`). Purgatorium never puts a sandbox to sleep on its own. Running sandboxes' web addresses do not go through Purgatorium: they keep working while it is down; waking needs it, and so do the TLS TCP addresses and Docker access (they go through Purgatorium's TCP gateway). `SANDBOX_MAX_TOTAL` (default 200) caps the running sandboxes on the whole server, the admin's included (asleep ones take no place): when it is reached nobody but the admin can create one or wake one (*The server is full*). The sign-in page shows the sandbox places above the sign-in buttons (taken and free; `LOGIN_CAPACITY=off` hides them), and once signed in the top bar does, on every page (e.g. *142 / 200 places*, the free ones on hover; orange from 90%, red when full). The **Overview** page shows the counts as cards: running of how many allowed, asleep, deep sleep and archived; for the admin the sandbox places used against the server limit (the admin's own sandboxes take places too), the host's CPU and memory (used now and reserved by running sandboxes), the disk use, a table per owner and a **Users** table. Users lists every account that has signed in (by e-mail; `admin` for the local admin): when it was last seen (a page load, at most every 10 minutes), its last sign-in and how many, its sandboxes now and created, and its last API use (its tokens); *no sandbox yet* marks someone who signed in but never created one. The rows are kept in `data/user-stats.json` until the admin deletes one (**Delete**: only the row; the account and its sandboxes stay). Only the admin sees them (`GET /users`, `DELETE /users/:account`).

From **My area → Access tokens** (`/settings/tokens`), a signed-in user can mint a personal access token (`p9m_…`) for their own agents to use as `Authorization: Bearer p9m_…`; the token acts as that user for the API. The full token is shown once, at creation. Tokens can be set to expire in 30 days, 90 days, or never, and can be revoked at any time.

A token can also be limited to one sandbox (**Access** in the dialog, or **Token for this sandbox…** on a sandbox panel's **Access** tab). Such a token lists and opens only that sandbox, and can start, stop and restart it and change its sleep times; it cannot create or delete sandboxes or manage tokens (403), and any other sandbox answers 404. Deleting the sandbox leaves the token in place: if you restore the sandbox, it works again.

With such a token an agent can deploy and update apps in the user's sandbox: the Purgatorium API gives it the sandbox's Docker client certificates, and the `docker` command line reaches the sandbox's own Docker daemon (or, in a sandbox from the `portainer` template, the Portainer API). Step by step: [agent guide](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/agent-guide/index.md).

## Simple and Advanced

The top bar has a **Simple | Advanced** switch, remembered for each account (users start in Simple, the admin in Advanced). Users have it only with `USER_VIEW_SWITCH=true`; by default they stay in Simple, see [Configuration](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/configuration/index.md). Simple is for people who only want their app online: the menu shows *My area* only (your sandboxes, without its tabs); the list shows the name, status, *Sleeps in* and age; a new sandbox asks for a name and a template; a sandbox panel has **Wake** or **Sleep**, an **Apps** tab (the web address of each app and **Let your agent deploy…**: the Claude Code plugin or a zip for other agents, the same window as in Advanced, which adds its **Options**) and a **Details** tab (when it last ran, the sleep times, warnings, archiving). Advanced shows everything: Overview, tokens, SSH keys, the Terminal and Logs, and the Containers, Access, Files, Resources and Registry tabs. Simple only hides: what an account may do is the same in both, and the API and MCP do not change. `PUT /me/view` with `{"view": "simple"}` or `{"view": "advanced"}` sets it (403 for a user without `USER_VIEW_SWITCH=true`); `GET /me` returns it as `view`, and whether the account may switch as `view_switch`.

## Light and dark

The pages follow the device's light or dark setting until the account chooses one with the sun / moon button in the top bar; the choice is remembered for the account, so it holds on any computer. The sign-in page, before anyone is signed in, always follows the device. The page shown while a sandbox wakes up, the error pages, the terminal and the log view stay dark. `PUT /me/theme` with `{"theme": "light"}`, `"dark"` or `"system"` sets it; `GET /me` returns it as `theme` (`null`: the device decides).

## Host folders

The admin can mount folders of the host into a sandbox, e.g. a shared data folder, when `HOST_MOUNT_ROOTS` lists where they may come from (e.g. `HOST_MOUNT_ROOTS=/srv/shared`; see [Configuration](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/configuration/index.md)). On a sandbox panel's **Resources** tab, **Host folders** lists them, with **Remove** for each, and a form to add one: the host folder (at or under one of the roots), where it appears in the sandbox (empty: `/mnt/<last part of the host path>`) and **read-only**. The folder is bind-mounted into the sandbox container, so the apps in the sandbox's own Docker can bind it from there too (e.g. `/mnt/shared:/data`).

Adding or removing one recreates the sandbox container, after a confirmation: a running sandbox restarts (its apps are unreachable for a few seconds), an asleep one stays asleep, one in deep sleep gets the change when it wakes. A host folder that does not exist is not created: Docker refuses it, the panel shows Docker's message and nothing changes. The target cannot be `/`, a system directory (`/etc`, `/usr`, `/proc`, `/dev`, `/run`…) or on, above or under one of the sandbox's own mounts (`/var/lib/docker`, `/opt`, `/root`, `/home`, `/srv`, …). The mounts are kept in the sandbox's compose file (and its `p9m.mounts` label), so they survive sleep, deep sleep and upgrades.

**A mount gives whoever owns the sandbox that host folder**, as root, and every app and agent in it: mount read-only what they need not change, and only what they may see. The owner sees the list on the **Resources** tab, in Simple on **Details** (read-only); only the admin adds or removes them. With `HOST_MOUNT_ROOTS` unset no mount can be added; ones already there stay until the admin removes them. API: `GET`, `POST` and `DELETE /sandboxes/:name/mounts` (see [API](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/api/index.md)), over MCP `list_sandbox_mounts`, `add_sandbox_mount` and `remove_sandbox_mount`.

# Runtimes and templates

A sandbox is a **runtime** (how it runs) plus a **template** (what runs inside), picked separately on create (`runtime`, `template`; the **New sandbox** form has a select for each):

| Runtime  | Isolation                                  | Use                                                                               |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dind`   | `privileged: true`                         | development, any Docker host (incl. Docker Desktop / WSL)                         |
| `sysbox` | `runtime: sysbox-runc`, no privileged mode | production; requires [sysbox](https://github.com/nestybox/sysbox) on a Linux host |

| Template            | What runs inside                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `starter` (default) | a hello app; deploy yours with `docker`, SSH or an agent                                                                                                                                                |
| `portainer`         | the same with Portainer, a web UI for the sandbox's Docker (its address and password in the API and the panel; it runs with `-H unix:///var/run/docker.sock`, so its environment exists from the start) |
| `tcp-demo`          | a demo of [TLS TCP addresses](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/networking/#tls-tcp-addresses): Postgres, Redis, SSH and pgweb                                                                     |
| `empty`             | nothing: paste your own compose file in the dialog                                                                                                                                                      |

Both runtimes have the same wiring (FRP tunnel, Traefik route, Sablier sleep/wake, `docker_data` volume, archive on delete). The sysbox image runs plain `dockerd`, so its TLS listener is configured through the runtime's `daemon_json` field, which Purgatorium merges into the generated `daemon.json`. Both run in production. On a shared server use `sysbox` only: install it on the host and set `ALLOWED_RUNTIMES=sysbox` (see [Security](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/security/index.md)).

**Runtimes** are `runtimes/<name>.yaml`: a `description`, the sandbox's own `docker_compose` (the DinD container, frps, socat, and their Traefik and Sablier labels) and an optional `daemon_json`. **Templates** are directories, `templates/<name>/`:

- `compose.yaml` (required): the stack deployed into the sandbox's own Docker on creation, a plain compose file.
- `template.yaml` (optional, every field optional): `description` (default: the directory name), `before_script` (JavaScript run on create; what it returns becomes `${variables}` for both compose files and the sandbox's `extras`, e.g. a generated password), `idle_timeout` (Go duration, default `30m`: how long a sandbox may go without HTTP traffic before it sleeps; a create request can override it), `deep_sleep_after` (default `7d`), `inner_project_name` (default `inner`).

A new template is a new directory; it shows up in `GET /templates` and the form without a restart. In both files Purgatorium fills in `${name}`, `${raw_name}`, `${host_domain}`, `${template_name}`, `${runtime_name}` and whatever `before_script` returned; any other `${…}` is left for docker compose (write `$$` for a literal `$`). Publish a port on all interfaces (`"5432:5432"`) to give it a link and a [TLS TCP address](https://csakaszamok.github.io/p9m/0.12/networking/#tls-tcp-addresses); a port on `127.0.0.1` stays private to the sandbox; a `p9m.connect.user` label puts its login into the **Connect…** commands.
